title: NBA Offseason Digest
subtitle: September 19, 2026: Young Stars Secure Extensions, Kawhi Returns to Toronto

items.headline: Jazz Lock Up Keyonte George with $157.5M Extension
items.summary: Utah Jazz guard Keyonte George has agreed to a five-year, $157.5 million rookie-scale contract extension, securing a cornerstone piece for the franchise. The 22-year-old had a breakout 2025-26 season, averaging 23.6 points, 6.1 assists, and 3.7 rebounds.

items.headline: Thompson Twins Make History with $100M+ Extensions
items.summary: Ausar and Amen Thompson have become the first brothers in NBA history to each sign contracts worth over $100 million. Ausar secured a five-year, $155 million rookie-scale extension with the DET Pistons, while Amen signed a five-year, $208 million extension with the HOU Rockets earlier this month.

items.headline: Kawhi Leonard Officially Returns to TOR Raptors
items.summary: Kawhi Leonard has officially returned to the Toronto Raptors after the NBA approved a trade with the LA Clippers. The deal, which was delayed by a league investigation, sends Leonard back to the team he won a championship with in 2019, alongside Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, draft picks, and swaps going to the Clippers.

items.headline: MIA Heat Sign Pelle Larsson to $60M Extension
items.summary: The Miami Heat have agreed to a four-year, $60 million contract extension with guard Pelle Larsson. Larsson, a 2024 second-round pick, emerged as a vital rotation player, starting 54 of 70 games last season and averaging 11.4 points, 3.5 rebounds, and 3.4 assists.

items.headline: Jalen Duren's Contract Talks with DET Hit Stalemate
items.summary: Despite Ausar Thompson's extension, Jalen Duren remains a restricted free agent with contract negotiations at a standstill between him and the Detroit Pistons. Duren, an All-NBA Third Team selection, is reportedly seeking to maximize his market value, but the Pistons are hesitant after his 2026 playoff performance.

items.headline: Stephen Curry Confirms Attempt to Recruit LeBron James to GSW
items.summary: Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry confirmed he personally attempted to recruit LeBron James to the team during the 2026 offseason, stating, 'If anybody didn't try, I think they'd be a fool.' James had become the biggest name on the free-agent market after leaving the Lakers.

items.headline: Kings' High Asking Price Stalls Sabonis Trade
items.summary: A potential trade for SAC Kings center Domantas Sabonis remains uncertain, with the Kings' steep asking price being a key obstacle for teams like the CHA Hornets. Sabonis, who has two years and $94 million left on his current deal, is also reportedly interested in a new max contract.

items.headline: LAL Lakers Eying Derrick Jones Jr. Amid Clippers Fallout
items.summary: The LA Lakers are reportedly targeting Derrick Jones Jr. from the LA Clippers, who are looking to recoup draft capital after being stripped of five first-round picks. Jones Jr., a defensive wing on an expiring $10.4 million contract, could be a low-cost addition for the Lakers.

items.headline: Deni Avdija Not Cleared for FIBA Qualifiers Due to Back Injury
items.summary: Portland Trail Blazers forward Deni Avdija was not cleared by his team to play for Israel in the recent FIBA World Cup qualifiers due to a complex back injury that bothered him last season. Avdija, a 2025-26 All-Star who averaged 24.2 points, 6.9 rebounds, and 6.7 assists, prioritized his recovery.

items.headline: Luka Doncic Expected Back in Los Angeles Tomorrow
items.summary: Lakers star Luka Doncic is expected to return to Los Angeles on September 20, ending his extended stay in Slovenia. This will give him eight days to prepare before the Lakers' media day on September 28 and training camp on September 29.

items.headline: DAL Mavericks Finalize Coaching Staff Under Dusty May
items.summary: The Dallas Mavericks have announced their full coaching staff for the 2026-27 season under new head coach Dusty May. Former Pelicans head coach Willie Green will serve as lead assistant, alongside newly retired 16-year veteran Garrett Temple, Joe Boylan, Drew Williamson, Mody Maor, Rob Fodor, and Sam Hershberger.

items.headline: CHI Bulls Announce Tiago Splitter's Coaching Staff
items.summary: The Chicago Bulls have finalized Tiago Splitter's first-ever coaching staff. Key hires include Blake Ahearn, Rex Kalamian, and Jamelle McMillan, with McMillan bringing significant player development experience from his time with the Pistons' G-League affiliate.

items.headline: Stephen Silas Joins TOR Raptors Coaching Staff
items.summary: Former Rockets head coach Stephen Silas has joined Darko Rajakovic's coaching staff for the Toronto Raptors. Silas, who previously coached the Rockets from 2020-2023, brings extensive assistant coaching experience from several NBA teams.

items.headline: PHI 76ers Big Man Adem Bona Suffers Foot Sprain
items.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers announced an early injury blow ahead of the 2026-27 season, with MRI results confirming that reserve big man Adem Bona has suffered a left foot sprain. He will be reevaluated before the team's training camp.
